text.p: The Bell Canadian Open was reduced to 54 holes after only three hours of play on Saturday due to torrential rain.
The downpoar, courtesy of the remnants of Hurricane Fran, flooded the Glen Abbey course, stopping play even before the second round leaders had teed off.
Officials rescheduled the third round to resume early on Sunday, but the dreadful forecast suggested such a scenario was a little optimistic.
Under PGA Tour rules, the championship could be cut to 36 holes and remain official, in which case Scott Dunlap would win.
Dunlap, a 33-year-old tour rookie, posted a 15-under-par 129 total on Friday after rounds of 64 65.
He led by three strokes from fellow American Dudley Hart, and was five shots clear of anyone else.
Mike Shea, the tournament director for the PGA Tour, refused to rule out a Monday finish, if that proved necessary to complete 54 holes, but nor did he say such a scenario was likely.
